### `todo_app_guests`

Temporary guest accounts identified by device fingerprint for anonymous
access to the todo application.

Guest accounts enable unauthenticated users to interact with the system
without email/password credentials. Each guest is uniquely identified by
a device fingerprint that persists across sessions. Guest accounts
support soft delete for data retention policies and can be converted to
member accounts through registration flows.

Guests have limited permissions compared to members, primarily focused on
exploring the application before committing to account creation.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key for guest account records.
- `device_fingerprint`
  > Unique device identifier for guest authentication.
  >
  > This fingerprint is generated from browser/device characteristics and
  > serves as the guest's identity across sessions. It enables persistent
  > anonymous access without requiring email or password credentials. The
  > fingerprint must be unique to prevent guest identity collisions.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the guest account was first created.
  >
  > This field records when the guest first accessed the application and was
  > assigned a device fingerprint. Used for tracking guest account age and
  > session history analysis.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when the guest account was last modified.
  >
  > This field is updated whenever guest account metadata changes, such as
  > session activity or device fingerprint updates.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when the guest account was soft deleted.
  >
  > When set, the guest account is marked as deleted but retained in the
  > database. This supports data retention policies and allows for potential
  > account recovery or audit trail preservation.

### `todo_app_guest_sessions`

Temporary session tokens for guest authentication without credentials.

This table manages guest login sessions for users who access the todo
application anonymously. Each session is tied to a specific guest account
and tracks authentication state, access context, and session validity
period.

Guest sessions enable temporary access to the application without
requiring email/password registration. They are used for previewing
features or testing the application before committing to account
creation.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each guest session.
- `todo_app_guest_id`
  > Foreign key to the guest account this session belongs to.
  >
  > This establishes the relationship between a session and its owning guest.
  > Each guest can have multiple active sessions across different devices or
  > browsers. The session is invalidated when the guest account is deleted.
- `ip`
  > IP address from which the guest session was created.
  >
  > This field records the network address of the client device at login
  > time. It is used for security auditing, session anomaly detection, and
  > access logging.
- `href`
  > URL of the page where the guest session was initiated.
  >
  > This field captures the entry point URL when the guest authentication
  > occurred. It helps track user flow patterns and session origins.
- `referrer`
  > Referrer URL that led to the session creation page.
  >
  > This field records the previous page URL that directed the user to the
  > session initiation point. Useful for analytics and user journey tracking.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the guest session was created.
  >
  > This field marks the start time of the session. It is used to calculate
  > session age, enforce expiration policies, and sort sessions
  > chronologically.
- `expired_at`
  > Timestamp when the guest session expires.
  >
  > This field defines the validity period of the session. Guest sessions
  > have a limited lifetime for security purposes. Sessions past this
  > timestamp are considered invalid and require re-authentication.

### `todo_app_members`

Registered member accounts with email and password authentication
credentials.

This table stores authenticated user accounts that can create, manage,
and delete their own todos. Each member has a unique email for login, a
password hash for authentication, and a display name for profile
identification. Members own todos and edit histories in the todo domain.

Members can change their password through the password reset flow managed
by [todo_app_member_password_resets](#todo_app_member_password_resets). Active login sessions are
tracked in [todo_app_member_sessions](#todo_app_member_sessions). When a member deletes their
account, all their todos (including those in trash) are permanently
deleted.

Properties as follows:

- `id`
  > Primary Key for member account identification.
  >
  > This UUID uniquely identifies each registered member account across the
  > system. It is used as a foreign key reference in related tables such as
  > [todo_app_todos](#todo_app_todos) and [todo_app_member_sessions](#todo_app_member_sessions).
- `email`
  > Unique email address used for member authentication and account
  > identification.
  >
  > This field serves as the primary login credential alongside the password.
  > It must be unique across all members to ensure proper authentication. The
  > email is used for password reset flows and account recovery.
- `password_hash`
  > BCrypt hashed password for member authentication.
  >
  > The password is hashed using BCrypt algorithm before storage to ensure
  > security. The hash is compared during login authentication to verify
  > member credentials. Members can change their password through the
  > password reset flow.
- `display_name`
  > Display name shown in the user's profile and todo lists.
  >
  > This is a user-friendly name that appears in the UI instead of the email
  > address. Members can edit their display name at any time. The display
  > name is not required to be unique across members.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the member account was created.
  >
  > This field is set automatically when a new member registers and cannot be
  > modified. It represents the account creation date and is used for sorting
  > and filtering member accounts.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when the member account was last updated.
  >
  > This field is updated automatically whenever any member profile
  > information is modified, including display name changes or password
  > updates. It tracks the most recent modification to the account.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when the member account was soft deleted.
  >
  > This field is set when a member deletes their account. Soft deletion
  > allows for account recovery within a retention period. When deleted, all
  > associated todos (including those in trash) are permanently deleted. A
  > null value indicates the account is active.

### `todo_app_member_sessions`

JWT session tokens for member authentication with access and refresh
support.

This table manages active login sessions for authenticated members. Each
session is created when a member successfully logs in and remains active
until the member logs out or deletes their account. Sessions are isolated
per user and validated on every authenticated request to ensure secure
access to todos and profile data.

Session lifecycle: Created on successful login, terminated on logout or
account deletion. Invalid or expired sessions are rejected immediately.
The expired_at field ensures sessions have a maximum lifetime for
security purposes.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each member session.
- `todo_app_member_id`
  > Foreign key to the member account that owns this session.
  >
  > This establishes the relationship between a session and its owning
  > member. Each session belongs to exactly one member, and a member can have
  > multiple active sessions across different devices or browsers. The
  > session is terminated when the member logs out or deletes their account.
- `ip`
  > IP address from which the member logged in.
  >
  > Records the network address used during authentication for security
  > auditing and session validation purposes.
- `href`
  > URL where the login occurred.
  >
  > Captures the entry point URL during the authentication flow for tracking
  > and security purposes.
- `referrer`
  > Referrer URL indicating where the user came from before logging in.
  >
  > Tracks the source page that led to the login page for analytics and
  > security monitoring.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the session was created.
  >
  > Records the exact time when the member successfully authenticated and the
  > session was established.
- `expired_at`
  > Timestamp when the session expires.
  >
  > Sets the maximum lifetime for the session for security purposes. Sessions
  > are validated against this timestamp on every request to ensure they
  > haven't exceeded their allowed duration.

### `todo_app_member_password_resets`

Password reset tokens with expiration for member account recovery.

This table stores temporary password reset tokens generated when a member
requests to reset their password. Each token is associated with a
specific member account and has an expiration time. Tokens are used to
verify the member's identity during the password reset process.

Tokens are created when a member requests a password reset and become
invalid after expiration or after successful password change. Multiple
tokens can exist for the same member if multiple reset requests are made.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_app_member_id`
  > References the member account requesting password reset.
  >
  > This foreign key establishes the relationship between a password reset
  > token and the member account it belongs to. Each password reset is tied
  > to exactly one member.
- `token`
  > Secure random token for password reset verification.
  >
  > This token is sent to the member's email and must be provided when
  > setting a new password. It serves as proof that the person resetting the
  > password has access to the account's email address.
- `expired_at`
  > Expiration timestamp for the password reset token.
  >
  > Tokens become invalid after this time. The expiration is typically set to
  > a short duration (e.g., 1 hour) for security purposes.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the password reset token was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the password reset record was last updated.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when the password reset record was soft deleted.
  >
  > Nullable field for soft delete support. Deleted tokens are no longer
  > valid for password resets.

### `todo_app_todos`

Core task items owned by members with title, description, optional dates,
completion status, and soft delete support.

Each todo represents a single task item that a member can create, track,
and manage throughout its lifecycle. Todos support completion toggling,
editing with history tracking, and soft deletion with trash
functionality.

Todos are filtered by completion status (all/complete/incomplete) and
sorted by creation date, start date, or due date. All todos are private
to their owning member with no cross-user visibility.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key for todo items.
- `todo_app_member_id`
  > References the member who owns this todo.
  >
  > Each todo belongs to exactly one member. The member has full CRUD access
  > to their own todos and cannot access other members' todos. When a member
  > deletes their account, all their todos are permanently deleted.
- `title`
  > Required title of the todo item.
  >
  > The title is the primary identifier for a todo and is required at
  > creation. It appears in todo lists and can be edited by the member.
- `description`
  > Optional detailed description of the todo item.
  >
  > Members can provide additional context or details about the task. This
  > field can be left empty or updated at any time.
- `start_date`
  > Optional start date for the todo item.
  >
  > Members can set when a task should begin. When sorting by start date,
  > todos without this value appear at the end.
- `due_date`
  > Optional due date for the todo item.
  >
  > Members can set a deadline for task completion. When sorting by due date,
  > todos without this value appear at the end.
- `completed`
  > Completion status of the todo item.
  >
  > Todos are incomplete (false) by default. Members can toggle between
  > complete and incomplete states. This field is used for filtering todos by
  > completion status.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the todo was created.
  >
  > Recorded automatically at todo creation. Used for sorting todos by
  > creation date (newest or oldest first).
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when the todo was last modified.
  >
  > Updated automatically on every edit operation. Each edit also creates an
  > entry in todo_app_todo_edit_histories.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when the todo was soft deleted.
  >
  > When set, the todo moves to trash and no longer appears in normal todo
  > lists. Members can restore the todo (clear this field) or permanently
  > delete it (removes todo and all edit history).

### `todo_app_todo_edit_histories`

Immutable audit trail recording all modifications to todos.

Each entry captures when an edit occurred and what field values were
changed to. This table provides a complete history of all changes made to
a todo's title, description, start date, and due date.

When a todo is permanently deleted, all its edit history entries are
cascade-deleted. History entries are sorted from most recent to oldest
when viewed by users.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_app_todos_id`
  > Foreign key to the todo being edited.
  >
  > Links this edit history entry to its parent todo. All edit histories for
  > a todo can be retrieved by filtering on this field.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when this edit was made.
  >
  > Records the exact moment the todo modification occurred. Used for sorting
  > history entries from most recent to oldest.
- `title_changed_to`
  > New title value after the edit.
  >
  > Contains the title value that the todo was changed to during this edit.
  > Null if title was not modified in this edit.
- `description_changed_to`
  > New description value after the edit.
  >
  > Contains the description value that the todo was changed to during this
  > edit. Null if description was not modified in this edit.
- `start_date_changed_to`
  > New start date value after the edit.
  >
  > Contains the start date value that the todo was changed to during this
  > edit. Null if start date was not modified in this edit.
- `due_date_changed_to`
  > New due date value after the edit.
  >
  > Contains the due date value that the todo was changed to during this
  > edit. Null if due date was not modified in this edit.

# Multi-User Todo Application API Requirements

## User Account Endpoints
- Sign up with email and password
- Log in with email and password
- Change password
- Delete account (all todos including trash are permanently deleted)

## User Profile Endpoints
- Get current user's profile
- Edit display name

## Todo Creation Endpoints
- Create a todo with:
  - Title (required)
  - Description (optional)
  - Start date (optional)
  - Due date (optional)
- Newly created todos are incomplete by default

## Todo Listing Endpoints
- View list of user's own todos (paginated)
- Each todo shows: title, completion status, start date (if set), due date (if set), creation date
- View single todo to see all details including full description

## Todo Completion Endpoints
- Mark a todo as complete
- Mark a todo as incomplete
- Toggle between complete/incomplete states

## Todo Editing Endpoints
- Edit todo's title, description, start date, and due date
- Every edit is recorded in history

## Edit History Endpoints
- View full edit history of a todo
- History entries sorted from most recent to oldest
- Each entry records: when edited, what changed (title, description, start date, due date)

## Todo Deletion Endpoints
- Delete own todos (soft delete)
- Deleted todos don't appear in normal list

## Trash Endpoints
- View list of deleted todos (paginated)
- Restore deleted todo from trash
- Permanently delete todo from trash (also deletes edit history)

## Filtering Endpoints
- Filter todo list by completion status:
  - All todos
  - Only complete todos
  - Only incomplete todos

## Sorting Endpoints
- Sort todo list by:
  - Creation date (newest first or oldest first)
  - Start date (earliest first or latest first)
  - Due date (earliest first or latest first)
- Todos without start date appear at end when sorting by start date
- Todos without due date appear at end when sorting by due date

## Privacy
- All endpoints are user-specific
- Users can only access their own data
- Authentication required for all endpoints

operations.specification:
1. Extract deviceFingerprint from request body
2. Check if guest with this deviceFingerprint already exists in todo_app_guests table
3. If exists, update lastActiveAt timestamp; if not, create new guest record with current timestamp
4. Generate JWT access token and refresh token with guest identity
5. Create session record in todo_app_guest_sessions with tokens and expiration
6. Return tokens in IAuthorized response format

Edge cases:
- Handle duplicate device fingerprints gracefully by reusing existing guest
- Ensure tokens have appropriate expiration times
- Validate deviceFingerprint format if constraints exist
operations.description:
Register a new guest user or activate an existing guest session using device fingerprint.

This operation allows unauthenticated visitors to create a temporary guest account identified by their device fingerprint. The guest can then access the todo application without email/password credentials. If a guest with the same device fingerprint already exists, their session is reactivated.

The guest identity is stored in the todo_app_guests table with the deviceFingerprint field. Session tokens are managed in the todo_app_guest_sessions table with access and refresh token support.

No authentication is required to call this endpoint since it is the entry point for unauthenticated users.

requestBody.description: Guest registration request containing device fingerprint identifier

responseBody.description: Authorization response containing access and refresh tokens for guest session

operations.name: join

operations.specification:
1. Extract refreshToken from request body
2. Validate refresh token signature and expiration
3. Look up guest session in todo_app_guest_sessions table using refresh token
4. Verify session is still valid and not expired
5. Generate new access token and refresh token pair
6. Update session record in todo_app_guest_sessions with new tokens and expiration
7. Return new tokens in IAuthorized response format

Error handling:
- Return 401 if refresh token is invalid or expired
- Return 404 if session not found
- Return 403 if session has been revoked
operations.description:
Refresh the guest's authentication tokens to extend their session.

This operation allows guest users to obtain new access and refresh tokens using their existing valid refresh token. This extends the guest's session without requiring re-registration.

The refresh process validates the existing refresh token against the todo_app_guest_sessions table, generates new token pairs, and updates the session record with the new tokens and expiration times.

No authentication is required since the refresh token itself serves as proof of prior authentication.

requestBody.description: Token refresh request containing valid refresh token

responseBody.description: Authorization response containing new access and refresh tokens for extended guest session

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification:
1. Validate request body contains email and password fields.
2. Check if email already exists in todo_app_members table (unique constraint).
3. If email exists, return 409 Conflict error.
4. Hash the password using BCrypt algorithm.
5. Insert new record into todo_app_members table with email, password_hash, and current timestamp for created_at/updated_at.
6. Generate JWT access token and refresh token for the new member.
7. Create session record in todo_app_member_sessions table.
8. Return ITodoAppMember.IAuthorized with tokens.
operations.description:
Register a new member account with email and password credentials.

This operation creates a new authenticated user account in the todo_app_members table. The email address must be unique and not already associated with an existing account. Upon successful registration, the member is immediately authenticated and can access their private todos and profile.

**Validation Requirements**:
- Email must be unique across all members
- Password must be provided and cannot be empty
- Both email and password are required fields

**Account Creation**:
- The email field serves as the primary login credential
- Password is hashed using BCrypt algorithm for security
- Display name is optional and can be set later
- Account is created with current timestamp for created_at and updated_at fields

**Authentication Flow**:
- Upon successful registration, JWT access and refresh tokens are generated
- A session record is created in todo_app_member_sessions
- The member can immediately access todo functionality without additional login

requestBody.description: Registration credentials for new member account

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens for the newly registered member

operations.name: join

operations.specification:
1. Validate request body contains email and password fields.
2. Query todo_app_members table for matching email address.
3. If no member found with the email, return 401 Unauthorized error.
4. Compare provided password with stored password_hash using BCrypt verification.
5. If password doesn't match, return 401 Unauthorized error.
6. Check if member account is soft deleted (deleted_at is not null).
7. If account is deleted, return 401 Unauthorized error.
8. Generate JWT access token and refresh token.
9. Create session record in todo_app_member_sessions with IP, href, and referrer if available.
10. Return ITodoAppMember.IAuthorized with tokens.
operations.description:
Authenticate a member with existing email and password credentials.

This operation validates member credentials against the todo_app_members table and grants access to the todo application. The email must match an existing account and the password must be correct. Upon successful authentication, the member can access their private todos and profile.

**Authentication Requirements**:
- Email must match an existing account in the system
- Password must match the stored hash for the email
- Account must not be soft deleted

**Session Management**:
- A new session is created in todo_app_member_sessions table
- Session includes IP address, href, and optional referrer for security tracking
- Session remains active until logout or account deletion
- Session is validated on every authenticated request

**Access Control**:
- Upon successful login, member gains access to their own todos
- Member can view, create, edit, complete, and delete their todos
- Member can view and edit their own profile
- All access is isolated to the authenticated member's data only

requestBody.description: Login credentials for existing member account

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens for the authenticated member

operations.name: login

operations.specification:
1. Validate the refresh token from request body.
2. Verify the refresh token is valid and not expired.
3. Query todo_app_member_sessions table to find the associated session.
4. If session not found or expired, return 401 Unauthorized error.
5. Verify the member account still exists and is not deleted.
6. Generate new JWT access token and refresh token.
7. Update the session record with new expiration timestamp.
8. Return ITodoAppMember.IAuthorized with new tokens.
operations.description:
Renew authentication tokens for an existing member session.

This operation allows members to extend their authentication session without re-entering credentials. The refresh token is validated against the todo_app_member_sessions table to ensure the session is still active and valid.

**Token Renewal**:
- Validates the provided refresh token against active sessions
- Generates new access and refresh tokens
- Updates session expiration timestamp
- Maintains the same session context

**Session Validation**:
- Refresh token must be valid and not expired
- Associated session must exist in todo_app_member_sessions
- Member account must not be deleted
- Session must not have been terminated by logout

**Security Considerations**:
- Refresh tokens have a longer expiration than access tokens
- Each refresh operation updates the session expiration
- Invalid or expired refresh tokens result in 401 Unauthorized
- Members must log in again if their session is terminated

responseBody.description: Renewed authentication tokens for the member

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of member accounts with search and filtering capabilities.

This endpoint returns member profile summaries including email, display name, and account timestamps. Members can search for accounts by email or display name using partial matching. The list can be filtered by account status (active or deleted) and sorted by creation date, update date, email, or display name.

By default, only active (non-deleted) members are returned. To include soft-deleted accounts, set the include_deleted filter to true. This is useful for administrative purposes to review account deletion history.

All member data is private and accessible only to authenticated users. The password hash is never included in responses for security reasons.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query todo_app_members table with pagination and filtering support.

Apply search filters on email and display_name fields using case-insensitive partial matching.

Filter by account status: active (deleted_at IS NULL) or deleted (deleted_at IS NOT NULL).

Filter by date ranges: created_at and updated_at for account creation and modification tracking.

Support sorting by: created_at (default, descending), updated_at, email, display_name.

Return cursor-based pagination for large result sets with metadata (total count, page size, current page).

Exclude password_hash from all responses for security.

Default behavior excludes soft-deleted members unless explicitly requested via include_deleted flag.

Apply data isolation: only authenticated members can access this endpoint (no guest access).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of member summary records containing email, display name, and account timestamps optimized for administrative list displays.

requestBody.description: Search criteria including email and display name filters, account status filter, date range filters, sorting options, and pagination parameters.

operations.description:
Retrieves the complete profile information for a specific member account.

This endpoint returns full member profile details including display name, email address, and account timestamps. Members can only access their own profile information due to strict data isolation policies. The endpoint is used for profile viewing and display purposes within the application.

Authentication is required to access this endpoint. The system validates that the requesting member is authorized to view the requested profile, ensuring users cannot access other members' data.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the todo_app_members table for a single member record by UUID primary key.

1. Extract memberId from path parameter and validate UUID format
2. Query todo_app_members WHERE id = memberId AND deleted_at IS NULL
3. If no active record found, return 404 Not Found
4. Verify the authenticated member's ID matches the requested memberId (data isolation enforcement)
5. If IDs don't match, return 403 Forbidden
6. Return full member record excluding password_hash field for security
7. Include: id, email, display_name, created_at, updated_at

Error handling:
- 404 if member not found or account is soft-deleted
- 403 if member attempts to access another user's profile
- 401 if not authenticated

responseBody.description: Complete member profile information including account details and timestamps.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the member account to retrieve (global scope).
parameters.name: memberId

operations.description:
Update the current authenticated member's profile information, specifically the display name.

This endpoint allows members to modify their display name at any time. The display name is a user-friendly identifier that appears in the UI instead of the email address. Members can choose to provide a display name or leave it empty.

The update operation automatically records the modification timestamp. Only the currently authenticated member can update their own profile - attempts to access other members' profiles are denied.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update the current authenticated member's display name.

1. Verify the member is authenticated via session middleware.
2. Extract the member ID from the authenticated session.
3. Validate that display_name is not an empty string if provided (null is allowed).
4. Update the display_name field in todo_app_members table for the authenticated member.
5. Automatically update the updated_at timestamp to the current time.
6. Return the updated member record with all profile fields.

Error handling:
- Return 401 if member is not authenticated.
- Return 400 if display_name is an empty string (null is acceptable).
- Return 403 if member attempts to update another member's profile (should be prevented by authentication context).

responseBody.description: Updated member profile with the new display name and refreshed updated_at timestamp.

requestBody.description: Profile update payload containing the new display name. The display name can be set to a string value or null to clear it. Empty strings are not allowed.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of session records for the authenticated member with optional filtering and sorting.

This endpoint allows members to view their login session history, including IP addresses, login URLs, and session timestamps. Sessions are filtered to show only those belonging to the authenticated user. The response includes both active and expired sessions, with an indicator showing whether each session is currently active.

Filtering options include session status (active/expired), date ranges for session creation, and IP address or URL pattern matching. Sorting is available by creation date, expiration date, or network details. Results are paginated using cursor-based navigation for efficient handling of large session histories.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query todo_app_member_sessions table for the authenticated member's sessions.

1. Retrieve current member ID from active session context
2. Apply filtering on:
   - Status (active vs expired based on expired_at vs current time)
   - Date range (created_at between start and end dates)
   - IP address pattern matching
   - Href/referrer URL patterns
3. Apply sorting on:
   - created_at (default: newest first)
   - expired_at
   - ip or href (alphabetical)
4. Apply cursor-based pagination with page size limits
5. Return session summaries with id, ip, href, referrer, created_at, expired_at, and is_active flag
6. Exclude member_id from response (already known from context)

Error handling:
- Return 401 if no active session exists
- Return empty list if no sessions found matching criteria

responseBody.description: Paginated list of member session summary records optimized for administrative list displays.

requestBody.description: Search criteria including session status filter, creation date range, IP address patterns, URL patterns, and pagination parameters.

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific member session by its unique identifier.

This endpoint returns complete session details including the IP address used during login, the URL where authentication occurred, the referrer page, session creation timestamp, and expiration timestamp. Sessions are private and isolated per user.

Authentication is required to access this endpoint. Users can only retrieve their own session information. Attempts to access another user's session are rejected with a forbidden error.

The session ID is a UUID that uniquely identifies each authentication session. This endpoint is useful for session management, security auditing, and monitoring active login sessions.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query todo_app_member_sessions table for the session with matching id.

Validate that the authenticated member owns this session by checking todo_app_member_id matches the current user's ID. Reject with 403 Forbidden if ownership validation fails.

Return the complete session record including id, todo_app_member_id, ip, href, referrer, created_at, and expired_at fields.

Handle edge cases:
- Session not found: return 404 Not Found
- Session belongs to another user: return 403 Forbidden
- Session already expired: still return the record (for audit purposes)

Ensure authentication middleware validates the request has a valid session before processing.

responseBody.description: Complete member session record with authentication details, network information, and timestamps.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the member session to retrieve (global scope).
parameters.name: sessionId

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of password reset tokens for the authenticated member's account.

This operation allows members to view their password reset history with optional filtering by date ranges and expiration status. Each password reset token record includes the creation timestamp, expiration time, and current validity status.

The response includes pagination metadata for navigating through large result sets. Only password reset tokens belonging to the authenticated member are accessible, ensuring proper data isolation between users.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query todo_app_member_password_resets table filtering by the authenticated member's ID (todo_app_member_id).

Apply search filters from request body:
- Filter by created_at date range if specified
- Filter by expired_at date range if specified
- Filter by expiration status (expired vs active) if requested
- Filter by deletion status (deleted_at is null for active tokens)

Apply pagination parameters from request body (page number, page size).

Sort results by created_at descending (most recent first) by default.

Return paginated summary records with token_id, created_at, expired_at, and status fields.

Ensure data isolation by only returning tokens belonging to the authenticated member.

Handle edge cases: empty result set, pagination beyond available records, invalid date ranges.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of password reset token summary records with creation and expiration timestamps.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for password reset tokens including date range filters, expiration status, and pagination parameters.

operations.description:
Retrieves a specific password reset record by its unique identifier.

This endpoint returns the complete details of a password reset token, including the associated member account, token value, expiration timestamp, and creation/update timestamps. The operation is designed for administrative or debugging purposes to inspect password reset records.

Authentication is required to access this endpoint. The requesting user must have appropriate permissions to view password reset records. Soft-deleted records are excluded from results.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the todo_app_member_password_resets table for a record matching the provided resetId (UUID).

1. Validate that resetId is a valid UUID format
2. Execute SELECT query on todo_app_member_password_resets WHERE id = ? AND deleted_at IS NULL
3. Join with todo_app_members to include member information if needed
4. Return the password reset record with all fields: id, todo_app_member_id, token, expired_at, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at
5. Handle case where record not found (404 Not Found)
6. Handle case where record is soft-deleted (404 Not Found)
7. Ensure proper error handling for invalid UUID format

responseBody.description: Complete password reset record including token details, expiration, and timestamps.

parameters.name: resetId

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of todos for the authenticated member with optional filtering and sorting.

This endpoint returns todos owned by the authenticated user, supporting filtering by completion status (all, complete, incomplete) and sorting by creation date, start date, or due date. Results are paginated with cursor-based navigation for efficient browsing of large todo lists.

Todos are filtered to exclude soft-deleted items (deleted_at is null) unless explicitly requesting trash items through a separate endpoint. Each todo summary includes the title, completion status, optional dates, and creation timestamp.

Authentication is required. Users can only access their own todos with no cross-user visibility.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query todo_app_todos table with the following logic:

1. Filter by todo_app_member_id = authenticated user's ID (from session)
2. Filter by deleted_at IS NULL to exclude trashed todos
3. Apply completion status filter if provided in request (completed = true/false/null for all)
4. Apply sorting based on sort field and direction:
   - created_at: sort by created_at ASC/DESC
   - start_date: sort by start_date ASC/DESC, NULLs last
   - due_date: sort by due_date ASC/DESC, NULLs last
5. Apply pagination using cursor-based approach:
   - Use after cursor for forward pagination
   - Use limit for page size (default 20, max 100)
6. Return todo summaries with: id, title, completed, start_date, due_date, created_at
7. Include pagination metadata: has_next, next_cursor, total_count

Error handling:
- Return 401 if user not authenticated
- Return 400 for invalid filter/sort parameters
- Return empty list if no matching todos found

responseBody.description: Paginated list of todo summaries with pagination metadata for cursor-based navigation.

requestBody.description: Search criteria including completion status filter, sort field and direction, and pagination parameters (cursor and limit).

operations.description:
Retrieve complete details of a single todo item by its unique identifier.

This endpoint returns all information about a specific todo including its title, description, start date, due date, completion status, and creation/update timestamps. Only authenticated members can access this endpoint, and they can only retrieve todos that they own.

The todo must be in an active state (not soft-deleted) to be retrieved. Attempting to access a deleted todo or a todo belonging to another member will result in an error response.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query todo_app_todos table for a single record by id (UUID).

Authorization: Verify the authenticated member's ID matches todo_app_member_id field. Reject with 403 if ownership mismatch.

Query: SELECT * FROM todo_app_todos WHERE id = {todoId} AND todo_app_member_id = {currentMemberId} AND deleted_at IS NULL.

Validation: Return 404 if no matching todo found or if todo belongs to different member.

Response: Return complete todo object with all fields including id, title, description, start_date, due_date, completed, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at (null for active todos).

Error handling: Return 404 for non-existent todos, 403 for unauthorized access attempts.

responseBody.description: Complete todo object with all fields including title, description, dates, completion status, and timestamps.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the todo to retrieve (global scope)
parameters.name: todoId

operations.description:
Create a new todo item for the authenticated member.

This endpoint allows members to create new task items with a required title and optional description, start date, and due date. Newly created todos are automatically marked as incomplete and owned by the authenticated member.

The todo will appear in the member's todo list immediately after creation. All todos are private to their owning member with no cross-user visibility.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Insert new record into todo_app_todos table.

1. Extract todo_app_member_id from authenticated session context.
2. Validate title is provided and non-empty (required field).
3. Set completed to false (incomplete by default).
4. Set created_at and updated_at to current timestamp.
5. Set deleted_at to null (active todo).
6. Insert record with provided title, description, start_date, due_date values.
7. Return the created todo entity with all fields including generated id and timestamps.

Error handling:
- Return 400 if title is missing or empty.
- Return 401 if user is not authenticated.
- Validate date formats for start_date and due_date if provided.

responseBody.description: The newly created todo entity with all fields including generated id, timestamps, and default completion status.

requestBody.description: Todo creation data including required title and optional description, start date, and due date.

operations.description:
Update an existing todo's properties including title, description, start date, and due date.

This operation allows authenticated members to modify their own todo items. The title field is required and cannot be empty. Description, start date, and due date are optional and can be updated independently.

Every edit operation automatically creates a history entry in the todo's edit history, recording when the change occurred and what fields were modified. This provides a complete audit trail of all modifications.

Only the todo owner can edit it. Attempts to edit another member's todo are rejected. Deleted todos (those in trash) cannot be edited and must be restored first before modification.

The completion status is not modified by this operation—use the dedicated completion toggle endpoint for that purpose.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
1. Verify authentication and extract current member ID from session.
2. Query todo_app_todos table for the todo with matching id and todo_app_member_id (ownership check).
3. Validate that the todo exists and belongs to the authenticated member.
4. Validate that deleted_at is null (cannot edit permanently deleted or trashed todos).
5. Extract editable fields from request body: title, description, start_date, due_date.
6. Validate title is not empty (required field).
7. Update the todo record with provided values, automatically set updated_at to current timestamp.
8. Create a new entry in todo_app_todo_edit_histories recording the edit timestamp and changed fields.
9. Return the updated todo entity with all fields including the new updated_at value.
10. Handle errors: todo not found (404), unauthorized access (403), validation errors (400).

responseBody.description: Updated todo entity with all fields including the new updated_at timestamp.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the todo to update (UUID format, global scope)
parameters.name: todoId

requestBody.description: Editable properties of the todo including title (required), description (optional), start date (optional), and due date (optional).

prerequisites.description: The todo item must be created before it can be updated. The todoId parameter references an existing todo that must exist in the database.

operations.description:
Soft deletes a todo item by moving it to trash.

This operation performs a soft delete on the specified todo, marking it as deleted by setting the deleted_at timestamp. The todo is removed from the normal todo list view but retains all its data including title, description, dates, completion status, and edit history. The deleted todo can be restored from trash or permanently deleted later.

Only the todo's owning member can perform this operation. Attempting to delete another member's todo results in an authorization error. The todo must exist and belong to the authenticated user.

After soft deletion, the todo no longer appears in standard todo list queries but remains accessible through trash-specific endpoints.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification: Verify the authenticated member owns the todo by checking todo_app_member_id matches the current user's ID. If ownership verification fails, return 403 Forbidden. Query the todo_app_todos table for the todo with the given id. If not found, return 404 Not Found. Update the todo's deleted_at field to the current timestamp (NOW()). Do not modify any other fields. The edit history for this todo is preserved and not affected by soft deletion. Return 204 No Content on success. Do not cascade delete edit history entries - they remain intact for audit trail purposes.

parameters.description: UUID of the todo to soft delete. The todo must belong to the authenticated member.
parameters.name: todoId

prerequisites.description: Todo must be created before it can be soft deleted. The todoId parameter references a todo that must exist in the database.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of deleted todos in the user's trash.

This operation returns todos that have been soft-deleted (deleted_at is set) and belong to the authenticated user. Deleted todos retain all their original properties including title, description, dates, and completion status. The trash list is paginated and can be filtered by completion status.

Users can only access their own trash. Deleted todos do not appear in normal todo list views. Each todo in trash can be restored or permanently deleted through separate operations.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query todo_app_todos table with the following conditions:
1. Filter by todo_app_member_id matching the authenticated user's ID
2. Filter by deleted_at IS NOT NULL (soft-deleted items only)
3. Apply completion status filter from request body if provided (completed = true/false)
4. Apply pagination parameters (page, limit) from request body
5. Sort by deleted_at DESC (most recently deleted first) as default

Return paginated results with cursor-based or offset-based pagination.

Validation:
- Ensure user is authenticated
- Verify todo_app_member_id matches authenticated user
- Validate pagination parameters are positive integers

Error handling:
- Return 401 if user is not authenticated
- Return empty list if no deleted todos exist

responseBody.description: Paginated list of deleted todo summary records for trash display.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for trash listing including completion status filter and pagination parameters.

operations.description:
Restore a deleted todo from trash back to active state.

This operation restores a soft-deleted todo to its active state, making it visible again in the normal todo list. The restoration preserves the todo's current properties exactly as they were when deleted, including title, description, start date, due date, and completion status. All edit history is also preserved.

The todo must be in trash to be restored. Attempting to restore a todo that is already active (not in trash) will result in an error. Similarly, attempting to restore a todo that does not exist or has been permanently deleted will fail.

Only the todo's owner can restore it. Users cannot access or restore todos belonging to other users.
operations.name: restore
operations.specification:
Query todo_app_todos table by id parameter.

Verify the todo exists. If not found, return 404 Not Found.

Verify the todo belongs to the authenticated member by checking todo_app_member_id matches the current user's ID. If not, return 403 Forbidden.

Verify the todo is currently in trash by checking deleted_at is not null. If deleted_at is null (todo is active), return 409 Conflict with message indicating todo is not in trash.

Update the todo by setting deleted_at to null. This restores the todo to active state.

The update preserves all other properties: title, description, start_date, due_date, completed, created_at, updated_at.

The edit history in todo_app_todo_edit_histories is preserved and not modified.

Return the restored todo entity with all fields.

Handle edge cases:
- If todo has been permanently deleted (row doesn't exist), return 404 Not Found
- If todo is already active (deleted_at is null), return 409 Conflict
- If todo belongs to another user, return 403 Forbidden

responseBody.description: The restored todo entity with all properties preserved from when it was deleted.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the todo to restore from trash (global scope).
parameters.name: todoId

prerequisites.description: Todo must be created before it can be deleted and subsequently restored from trash. The todoId parameter references a todo that must exist in the database.

operations.description:
Permanently delete a todo from trash along with all its edit history.

This operation removes a todo that has been soft-deleted (moved to trash) from the system entirely. Unlike regular deletion which moves a todo to trash, this permanently removes the todo and cannot be undone.

The todo must be in the trash state (soft-deleted) to be permanently deleted. Attempting to permanently delete a todo that is still active will fail with an error.

All edit history associated with the todo is also permanently removed as part of this operation.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification: Verify the authenticated member owns the todo by checking todo_app_member_id matches the current user's ID. Validate that the todo is in trash state (deleted_at column is not null). If validation fails, return appropriate error (404 if not found or not in trash, 403 if not owned). Delete the todo record from todo_app_todos table. Delete all associated edit history records from todo_app_todo_edit_histories where todo_id matches the deleted todo. Return 204 No Content on successful deletion.

parameters.description: UUID of the todo to permanently delete from trash (global scope)
parameters.name: todoId

operations.description:
Retrieve paginated list of edit history entries for a specific todo item.

This endpoint returns all modifications made to a todo, including changes to title, description, start date, and due date. History entries are sorted from most recent to oldest by edit timestamp.

Each history entry records when the edit was made and what field values were changed to. Fields that were not modified in an edit do not appear in that entry.

Users can only access the edit history of todos they own. The todo must exist and belong to the authenticated user.

Authentication is required. Returns 403 if attempting to access another user's todo history.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query todo_app_todo_edit_histories table filtering by todo_app_todos_id from path parameter.

Apply pagination from request body (page, pageSize).

Sort results by created_at in descending order (most recent first) as per business requirement.

Return paginated list of edit history summaries.

Verify the authenticated user owns the todo (check todo_app_todos.todo_app_member_id matches current user).

Return 404 if todo not found or user doesn't own it.

Return 403 if user attempts to access another user's todo history.

Each history entry includes: id, created_at, and changed fields (title_changed_to, description_changed_to, start_date_changed_to, due_date_changed_to).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of edit history summary records sorted from most recent to oldest.

parameters.description: UUID of the todo whose edit history to retrieve (global scope)
parameters.name: todoId

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for edit history listing.

prerequisites.description: Todo must be created before its edit history can be retrieved. The todoId path parameter requires an existing todo resource.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single edit history entry for a specific todo item.

This operation returns detailed information about one edit operation performed on a todo, including the timestamp of the edit and all field values that were changed during that edit. Each history entry documents a single modification to the todo's title, description, start date, or due date.

Edit history entries are automatically created by the system whenever a user edits their todo. The history provides an audit trail of all changes made to the todo over time, allowing users to track what was modified and when.

Users can only access edit history for todos they own. Attempting to view history for another user's todo will result in an access denied error. History entries remain accessible even if the todo is in trash, until the todo is permanently deleted.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the todo_app_todo_edit_histories table for a single record matching the provided historyId and todo_app_todos_id (todoId).

First, verify that the authenticated user owns the todo by checking that todo_app_todos.todo_app_member_id matches the current user's ID. If ownership verification fails, return a 403 Forbidden error.

Then, verify that the edit history entry belongs to the specified todo by confirming todo_app_todo_edit_histories.todo_app_todos_id equals the provided todoId. If mismatch, return a 404 Not Found error.

Return the full history entry including: id, created_at (edit timestamp), title_changed_to, description_changed_to, start_date_changed_to, and due_date_changed_to fields. Fields that were not modified in the edit will be null.

If the history entry does not exist, return a 404 Not Found error.

If the todo has been permanently deleted (and cascade delete removed the history), return a 404 Not Found error.

responseBody.description: Full edit history entry containing the edit timestamp and all field values that were changed during the edit operation.

parameters.name: todoId

parameters.description: UUID of the specific edit history entry to retrieve (global scope)
parameters.name: historyId

access.description:
Short-lived JWT access token for authenticating API requests.

This token must be included in the Authorization header using the Bearer
scheme (e.g., `Authorization: Bearer {access}`) for all endpoints requiring
authentication. The token contains encoded claims including user identity,
roles, and permissions. Typically expires within 15-60 minutes for
security; use the refresh token to obtain a new access token when expired.

refresh.description:
Long-lived refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

Used to request new access tokens when the current access token expires,
allowing session continuation without re-authentication. Should be stored
securely and transmitted only to the token refresh endpoint. Typical
lifetime ranges from 7 to 30 days depending on security requirements.

ISO 8601 timestamp when the access token expires.

After this timestamp, the access token will be rejected by authenticated
endpoints. Clients should proactively refresh before expiration to maintain
seamless user experience. A common strategy is to refresh when remaining
time falls below 5 minutes. This timestamp is also embedded within the JWT
itself as the "exp" claim.

refreshable_until.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp indicating the absolute session expiration deadline.

Represents the latest possible time the refresh token can be used. Once
this timestamp is reached, the user must fully re-authenticate with
credentials. This defines the maximum session duration regardless of
activity. If refresh token rotation is enabled, this deadline may extend
with each successful refresh.

Provides a complete authentication token structure containing both access and
refresh tokens along with their respective expiration timestamps. This
dual-token pattern enables secure, stateless authentication with automatic
session renewal capabilities.

The access token is short-lived for security, while the refresh token allows
obtaining new access tokens without requiring the user to re-enter
credentials. This structure is automatically included in authentication
responses across all generated backend applications.

New due date value after this edit, or null if due date was not modified.

When this field contains a value, it represents the due date that the todo was changed to during this edit operation. When null, the due date field was not part of this particular modification.
due_date_changed_to.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from todo_app_todo_edit_histories.due_date_changed_to. Nullable - contains the new due date value if due date was modified in this edit, null otherwise.

ITodoAppTodoEditHistory.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a todo edit history entry showing what was changed and when.

Each entry records a single modification to a todo item, capturing the exact timestamp of the edit and which specific fields were updated. Nullable fields indicate whether that particular attribute was modified during this edit operation. This audit trail enables users to track the complete evolution of their todo items over time.
ITodoAppTodoEditHistory.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from todo_app_todo_edit_histories table. All six columns are included as they represent the complete edit history entry. Fields title_changed_to, description_changed_to, start_date_changed_to, and due_date_changed_to are nullable to indicate whether that specific field was modified in this edit operation. The todo_app_todos_id foreign key and todo relation are excluded as they are implicit from the API path parameter context (edit history is retrieved for a specific todo identified by path).

page.description:
Page number for pagination (1-indexed). Default is 1.

Specifies which page of results to retrieve when viewing password reset token history. Page numbering starts from 1, so the first page is page 1. If not provided, the server defaults to returning the first page of results.
page.x-autobe-specification: Pagination page number (1-indexed). Defaults to 1 if not provided. Used to retrieve specific page of password reset tokens. Server validates minimum value of 1.

limit.description:
Number of items per page. Default is 10, maximum is 100.

Controls how many password reset tokens are returned in each page of results. The default is 10 items per page, with a maximum of 100 items allowed. This helps manage response size and client-side rendering performance.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Number of items per page. Defaults to 10 if not provided. Must be between 1 and 100. Used to control how many password reset tokens are returned per page.

oneOf.description: Field to sort results by. Default is created_at.
Field to sort results by. Default is created_at.

sort.description:
Field to sort results by. Default is created_at.

Specifies which field to use when sorting password reset tokens in the list. Can be set to 'created_at' to sort by when the reset request was made, or 'expired_at' to sort by when the token expires. Defaults to sorting by creation date.
sort.x-autobe-specification: Field to sort results by. Allowed values: 'created_at' or 'expired_at'. Defaults to 'created_at' if not provided. Determines which timestamp column is used for sorting password reset tokens.

oneOf.description: Sort order direction. Default is desc (newest first).
Sort order direction. Default is desc (newest first).

order.description:
Sort order direction. Default is desc (newest first).

Determines whether results are sorted in ascending or descending order. When set to 'desc' (descending), the most recent password reset tokens appear first. When set to 'asc' (ascending), older tokens appear first. Defaults to descending order to show the newest reset requests first.
order.x-autobe-specification: Sort order direction. Allowed values: 'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending). Defaults to 'desc' if not provided. When sorting by created_at, descending shows newest first.

expired_before.description:
Filter tokens that expired before this timestamp. Optional.

Filters the password reset token list to only show tokens that expired before the specified date and time. This is useful for viewing expired reset tokens. The timestamp must be in ISO 8601 date-time format. If not provided, no expiration date filtering is applied.
expired_before.x-autobe-specification: Filter password reset tokens that expired before the specified timestamp. Maps to expired_at column with 'less than' comparison. Optional parameter for filtering by expiration date. Uses ISO 8601 date-time format.

expired_after.description:
Filter tokens that expired after this timestamp. Optional.

Filters the password reset token list to only show tokens that expired after the specified date and time. This is useful for viewing tokens that are still valid or recently expired. The timestamp must be in ISO 8601 date-time format. If not provided, no expiration date filtering is applied.
expired_after.x-autobe-specification: Filter password reset tokens that expired after the specified timestamp. Maps to expired_at column with 'greater than' comparison. Optional parameter for filtering by expiration date. Uses ISO 8601 date-time format.

ITodoAppMemberPasswordReset.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for retrieving a paginated list of password reset tokens for the authenticated member's account.

This type defines the query parameters for filtering, sorting, and paginating through password reset tokens. All fields are optional with default values applied server-side. The authenticated member can view their password reset history with various filtering options to find specific reset requests.
ITodoAppMemberPasswordReset.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: Request parameters for listing password reset tokens with pagination, sorting, and filtering capabilities. Query parameters are processed server-side to filter and sort the todo_app_member_password_resets table. The authenticated member's ID (from JWT) is used to filter results - only their own password reset tokens are returned. Pagination defaults to page 1 with 10 items per page. Sorting defaults to created_at descending. Date filters (expired_before, expired_after) filter by the expired_at column.

refreshToken.description:
Refresh token obtained from a previous member authentication.

This long-lived JWT token allows obtaining new access tokens without re-authentication. Must be a valid token from a previous /todoApp/auth/member/join or /todoApp/auth/member/refresh response.

**Token Validation**:
- The token is validated against the todo_app_member_sessions table to verify it hasn't expired or been revoked
- Token must contain valid claims for an active member session
- Invalid or expired tokens result in 401 Unauthorized response
refreshToken.x-autobe-specification: JWT refresh token obtained from previous member authentication response (ITodoAppMember.IAuthorized.token.refresh). This token is not stored as a database column - it is validated against the todo_app_member_sessions table by matching the token's embedded claims (member_id, session_id, expiration) against the session record. The token contains encoded claims including member identity, session identifier, and expiration timestamp. Upon validation, new token pair is generated and session record is updated.

ITodoAppMember.IRefresh.description:
Request body for refreshing member authentication tokens.

This DTO contains the refresh token obtained from a previous member authentication session (registration, login, or token refresh). The refresh token is validated against the todo_app_member_sessions table to generate new access and refresh token pairs, extending the member's session without requiring re-login.

**Token Requirements**:
- Must be a valid JWT token from a previous /todoApp/auth/member/join or /todoApp/auth/member/refresh response
- The token is validated against the todo_app_member_sessions table to verify it hasn't expired or been revoked
- No authentication is required for this endpoint since the refresh token itself serves as proof of prior authentication
ITodoAppMember.IRefresh.x-autobe-specification: Authentication request DTO for member token refresh operation. The refreshToken property is a JWT token obtained from a previous member authentication response (ITodoAppMember.IAuthorized). This token is validated against the todo_app_member_sessions table to verify: (1) the session exists and is active, (2) the refresh token has not expired, (3) the associated member account is not deleted. Upon successful validation, the server generates new access and refresh token pairs and updates the session record's expiration timestamp. No direct database table mapping - this is a request body DTO for authentication.

# Multi-User Todo Application Testing Requirements

## User Account Tests
- Test sign up with valid email and password
- Test sign up with invalid email format
- Test sign up with existing email
- Test login with valid credentials
- Test login with invalid credentials
- Test password change
- Test account deletion (verifies all todos and trash are deleted)

## User Profile Tests
- Test getting current user's profile
- Test editing display name
- Test that users cannot view other users' profiles

## Todo Creation Tests
- Test creating todo with required title
- Test creating todo with title and description
- Test creating todo with all fields (title, description, start date, due date)
- Test creating todo without title (should fail)
- Test that newly created todos are incomplete by default

## Todo Listing Tests
- Test paginated todo listing
- Test that todos show correct fields (title, completion status, dates)
- Test viewing single todo with full details
- Test that users can only see their own todos

## Todo Completion Tests
- Test marking todo as complete
- Test marking todo as incomplete
- Test toggling completion status

## Todo Editing Tests
- Test editing todo title
- Test editing todo description
- Test editing start date
- Test editing due date
- Test that edits are recorded in history

## Edit History Tests
- Test viewing edit history of a todo
- Test that history is sorted from most recent to oldest
- Test that history entries record all changed fields

## Todo Deletion Tests
- Test soft deletion of todo
- Test that deleted todos don't appear in normal list

## Trash Tests
- Test viewing deleted todos (paginated)
- Test restoring deleted todo
- Test permanent deletion from trash
- Test that permanent deletion removes edit history

## Filtering Tests
- Test filtering by "all" todos
- Test filtering by "complete" todos only
- Test filtering by "incomplete" todos only

## Sorting Tests
- Test sorting by creation date (newest first)
- Test sorting by creation date (oldest first)
- Test sorting by start date (earliest first)
- Test sorting by start date (latest first)
- Test that todos without start date appear at end
- Test sorting by due date (earliest first)
- Test sorting by due date (latest first)
- Test that todos without due date appear at end

## Privacy Tests
- Test that users cannot access other users' data
- Test authentication is required for all endpoints

scenario.draft: Test that a new guest can successfully register using a unique device fingerprint. The test should verify: 1) A new guest record is created in the system with the provided device fingerprint, 2) JWT access and refresh tokens are generated and returned in the IAuthorized response, 3) The response includes the guest's unique ID, 4) The tokens contain proper expiration timestamps (expired_at and refreshable_until), 5) The guest can use the access token to authenticate subsequent API requests. This validates the primary success path for guest authentication.

The test should: 1) First call the join endpoint with a specific device fingerprint to create a guest, 2) Call the join endpoint again with the same device fingerprint, 3) Verify that the same guest ID is returned in both responses, 4) Verify that new tokens are issued for the reactivated session, 5) Confirm that no duplicate guest records are created. This validates the edge case handling for duplicate device fingerprints.

scenario.draft:
Test the successful guest token refresh workflow.

1. First, register a guest using /todoApp/auth/guest/join with a device fingerprint to obtain initial access and refresh tokens.
2. Extract the refresh token from the join response.
3. Call /todoApp/auth/guest/refresh with the valid refresh token in the request body.
4. Verify the response contains:
   - New access token (different from original)
   - New refresh token (different from original)
   - Updated expired_at timestamp (extended from original)
   - Updated refreshable_until timestamp (extended from original)
   - Guest id remains the same as from join response
5. Verify the new tokens are valid JWTs with proper structure.
6. Confirm the guest session has been extended successfully without requiring re-registration.

This validates the primary success path for guest session extension.

dependencies.purpose: Register guest and obtain initial refresh token for testing refresh functionality

scenario.draft:
Test guest token refresh with an expired or invalid refresh token.

1. First, register a guest using /todoApp/auth/guest/join with a device fingerprint to obtain initial tokens.
2. Extract the refresh token from the join response.
3. Wait for the refresh token to expire (or use a deliberately invalid/malformed token).
4. Call /todoApp/auth/guest/refresh with the expired/invalid refresh token.
5. Verify the system returns an appropriate error response:
   - HTTP 401 status code for invalid/expired tokens
   - Error message indicating the token is invalid or expired
6. Verify no new tokens are issued.
7. Confirm the guest session cannot be extended with an invalid token.

This validates the error handling for expired refresh tokens, ensuring the system properly rejects invalid authentication attempts.

scenario.draft:
Test successful member registration with valid email and password credentials.

**Setup**:
- No prerequisites needed (this is the join operation itself that creates authentication)

**Test Steps**:
1. Send POST request to /todoApp/auth/member/join with valid email (e.g., "newuser@example.com") and password
2. Include required fields: href (current page URI) and referrer (referring page URI) for session tracking
3. Optionally include display_name field for profile customization

**Expected Results**:
1. HTTP 200 OK response
2. Response body contains ITodoAppMember.IAuthorized with:
   - id: UUID for the new member account
   - email: The registered email address
   - display_name: The provided display name or null if not provided
   - created_at: Current timestamp in ISO 8601 format
   - updated_at: Current timestamp in ISO 8601 format
   - deleted_at: null (account is active)
   - token: Object containing access, refresh, expired_at, and refreshable_until fields
3. New member record created in todo_app_members table with BCrypt-hashed password
4. New session record created in todo_app_member_sessions table
5. Member can immediately access todo functionality using the access token without additional login

**Business Logic Validation**:
- Verify password is hashed using BCrypt algorithm in database, not stored as plain text
- Verify email uniqueness constraint is enforced (no duplicate emails allowed)
- Verify JWT access token is short-lived for security
- Verify JWT refresh token allows session continuation without re-authentication
- Verify expired_at timestamp indicates when access token expires
- Verify refreshable_until timestamp indicates absolute session expiration deadline
- Verify session tracking includes href and referrer information for security monitoring
- Verify member account is immediately active and can access private todos and profile

**Expected Results**:
1. HTTP 200 OK response
2. Response body contains ITodoAppMember.IAuthorized with:
   - id: UUID for the new member account
   - email: The registered email address
   - display_name: The provided display name ("John Doe")
   - created_at: Current timestamp in ISO 8601 format

3. New member record created in todo_app_members table with the display name stored
4. Display name can be used in UI instead of email address for better user experience
5. Display name can be updated later through profile editing operations

**Business Logic Validation**:
- Verify display_name is stored correctly in the member profile
- Verify display_name appears in the authentication response
- Verify display_name is optional (can be null if not provided)
- Verify display_name can be customized separately from email authentication credential
- Verify member with display name has same access permissions as member without display name

scenario.draft:
Test successful member login with valid credentials.

**Prerequisites**:
1. First, register a new member account using /todoApp/auth/member/join with a unique email and password
2. The join operation will create the member record and return authentication tokens

**Test Steps**:
1. Call POST /todoApp/auth/member/login with the same email and password used during registration
2. Include required session context fields: href, referrer, and optionally ip
3. Verify the response returns ITodoAppMember.IAuthorized with:
   - Member identity (id, email, display_name, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at)
   - Authorization tokens (access, refresh, expired_at, refreshable_until)
4. Verify the access token is a valid JWT that can be used for authenticated requests
5. Verify the refresh token is present for session renewal
6. Verify expired_at timestamp is in the future
7. Verify refreshable_until timestamp is in the future
8. Verify deleted_at is null (account is active)

**Expected Outcome**:
- HTTP 200 OK response
- New session record created in todo_app_member_sessions
- Member can use the access token to authenticate subsequent API requests

scenario.draft:
Test login attempt with email that does not exist in the system.

**Prerequisites**:
1. First, register a new member account using /todoApp/auth/member/join with a unique email (e.g., user@example.com)
2. This establishes a baseline for testing with a different, non-existent email

**Test Steps**:
1. Call POST /todoApp/auth/member/login with an email address that was never registered (e.g., nonexistent@example.com)
2. Include any password value (it won't matter since the email doesn't exist)
3. Include required session context fields: href, referrer

**Expected Outcome**:
- HTTP 401 Unauthorized error
- The system should reject the login attempt because no member record exists with the provided email
- No session should be created
- No authentication tokens should be returned

**Business Rule Validation**:
- This tests the requirement: "If the email address does not exist in the system, the login request is rejected"
- This is a business logic failure, not an input validation error

2. Provide an incorrect password (different from the one used during registration)

**Business Rule Validation**:

Test searching and filtering member accounts by various criteria.

  - Member 1: email "john@example.com", display_name "John Doe", created recently
  - Member 2: email "jane@example.com", display_name "Jane Smith", created earlier
  - Member 3: email "bob@test.com", display_name "Bob Wilson", created in middle

6. **Combine filters:** Use search + date filter + sorting together

**Expected Results:**
- Search performs case-insensitive partial matching on both email and display_name
- Date range filters correctly narrow results
- Sorting works correctly for all supported fields (email, display_name, created_at, updated_at)
- Multiple filters can be combined

scenario.draft:
Test including soft-deleted member accounts in the results.

- Create 2 active member accounts
- Soft delete 1 member account (set deleted_at)
- Keep 1 member account active (deleted_at = null)

**Test Steps:**
1. **Default behavior (exclude deleted):** Call without include_deleted parameter
   - Verify only active member is returned (1 record)
   - Verify deleted member is NOT in results
2. **Include deleted members:** Call with include_deleted=true

   - Verify deleted member has deleted_at timestamp set

**Expected Results:**
- Default behavior excludes soft-deleted members (deleted_at IS NULL only)

- Deleted_at field correctly distinguishes between active and deleted accounts
- Sorting works correctly even with mixed active/deleted members

scenario.draft:
Test the primary workflow of updating a member's display name through the profile update endpoint.

**Prerequisites**:
1. Register a new member account using /todoApp/auth/member/join with valid email and password
2. The member is now authenticated with valid session tokens

**Test Steps**:
1. Call PUT /todoApp/member/member/profile with a request body containing {"display_name": "John Doe"}
2. Verify the response returns HTTP 200 OK
3. Verify the response body contains the updated member profile with:
   - The display_name field set to "John Doe"
   - The updated_at timestamp is refreshed to the current time
   - All other member fields (id, email, created_at, deleted_at) remain unchanged
4. Verify the deleted_at field is null (account is active)

**Business Rules Validation**:
- The display name is successfully updated for the authenticated member
- The updated_at timestamp is automatically refreshed
- The member can view their own updated profile information
- Authentication is enforced (only the authenticated member can update their profile)

scenario.draft:
Test the workflow of clearing a member's display name by setting it to null.

**Prerequisites**:
1. Register a new member account using /todoApp/auth/member/join with valid email and password
2. Optionally, first set a display name by calling PUT /todoApp/member/member/profile with {"display_name": "Some Name"}
3. The member is authenticated with valid session tokens

**Test Steps**:
1. Call PUT /todoApp/member/member/profile with a request body containing {"display_name": null}
2. Verify the response returns HTTP 200 OK
3. Verify the response body contains the updated member profile with:
   - The display_name field set to null
   - The updated_at timestamp is refreshed to the current time
   - All other member fields remain unchanged
4. Verify the member can successfully clear their display name

**Business Rules Validation**:
- Setting display_name to null is allowed and clears the display name
- The updated_at timestamp is automatically refreshed

instruction:
# Multi-User Todo Application Implementation Requirements

## User Account Implementation
- Implement sign up with email and password (validate email format, check for existing email, hash password)
- Implement login with email and password (validate credentials, return auth token)
- Implement password change (verify current password, update to new password)
- Implement account deletion (cascade delete all todos including trash and edit history)

## User Profile Implementation
- Implement getting current user's profile
- Implement editing display name
- Ensure users cannot view other users' profiles (authentication check)

## Todo Creation Implementation
- Implement creating todo with title (required), description (optional), start date (optional), due date (optional)
- Set newly created todos as incomplete by default
- Associate todo with authenticated user

## Todo Listing Implementation
- Implement paginated todo listing for current user only
- Include title, completion status, start date, due date, creation date in list response
- Implement viewing single todo with full details including description
- Ensure users can only see their own todos (authentication and authorization check)

## Todo Completion Implementation
- Implement marking todo as complete
- Implement marking todo as incomplete
- Implement toggle functionality
- Ensure only the todo owner can modify it

## Todo Editing Implementation
- Implement editing todo's title, description, start date, and due date
- Create edit history entry for every edit
- Record what changed in the history entry
- Ensure only the todo owner can edit it

## Edit History Implementation
- Implement viewing edit history of a todo
- Sort history from most recent to oldest
- Include all changed fields in history entries
- Ensure only the todo owner can view the history

## Todo Deletion Implementation
- Implement soft deletion (set deleted flag, don't remove from database)
- Deleted todos should not appear in normal todo list
- Ensure only the todo owner can delete it

## Trash Implementation
- Implement viewing deleted todos (paginated)
- Implement restoring deleted todo (unset deleted flag)
- Implement permanent deletion (remove from database including edit history)
- Ensure only the todo owner can access trash items

## Filtering Implementation
- Implement filtering by completion status: all, complete, incomplete
- Apply filter to todo list queries

## Sorting Implementation
- Implement sorting by creation date (newest/oldest first)
- Implement sorting by start date (earliest/latest first, nulls last)
- Implement sorting by due date (earliest/latest first, nulls last)
- Handle null dates correctly (appear at end when sorting by date)

## Privacy Implementation
- All endpoints require authentication
- All endpoints check that user owns the data they're accessing
- No cross-user data access possible
